seasons.review_body: Larry David and Jeff Schaffer turn America's 250th anniversary into a sketch-comedy target, improvising through the founding and early presidency the way Curb Your Enthusiasm improvised through David's own petty grievances. Reception landed mixed: 53% on Rotten Tomatoes across 30 critics, 58 on Metacritic from 24, both squarely average. AV Club's Erik Adams argued David is fit to encapsulate the era's contradictions, even if the show itself is unlikely to follow him into the history books. Other reviewers found the format strongest when it stays petty and specific, weaker when it reaches for earnest political relevance outside David's comfort zone. What works: the improvised, structural-outline format transplanted cleanly onto history. What strains: sketches that want to say something serious about the country rather than just something funny about people.
